subject: Budget range validation - monthly token spend & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@vyronpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick follow-up + budget band confirmation (post-demo)

Hi Chris — great to catch up this morning. Thanks for walking through Vyron's payments flows and the volume profile. As discussed, I wanted to recap the usage assumptions we heard and validate the monthly spend band so we can lock a pricing band for the PO/procurement conversation.

Summary of what we noted on the call:
- Peak use-case: authorization and settlement assistant for agents + automated reconciliation generation.
- Estimated request profile: 2–4M text-generation tokens/day during peak (production), ~40–90M tokens/month on average.
- Eval/QA/dev: additional ~10–20M tokens/month.
- Total expected monthly tokens: ~50–110M tokens.

Two asks so we can move to procurement:
1) Can you confirm whether the 50–110M monthly token range looks right for FY27 forecasting?
2) Procurement thresholds: what vendor approval band do we need (e.g., <$25k/month, $25–50k/month, $50k+)? Any required lead times for legal/finance review?

Pricing context (preliminary): attached is a v1 pricing estimate (PDF) with tiered unit economics. High-level guidance: depending on model family and any quantized variants we serve, net pricing typically ranges from ~$150 to $400 per 1M tokens for enterprise-managed dedicated deployments, with hosted API options at a slightly higher per-token rate but no long-term commit. For budgeting, a safe working target is $200–$300 per 1M tokens for initial forecasts.

Next steps I propose:
- You validate the monthly band + procurement approval threshold (Q) by EOD Tue 10/20.
- If OK, we’ll prep a commercial term sheet and a DocuSign SOW for procurement.

Attached: v1_pricing_estimate.pdf (pricing scenarios) and sample usage export format.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@vyronpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@vyronpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + budget band confirmation (post-demo)

Thanks for the clear recap, Rishi — appreciate it. Quick answers from our side: 

- Monthly band: the 50–110M tokens/month is aligned with our internal forecast for the first two quarters of rollout. The upper bound assumes aggressive agent adoption and additional reconciliation flows.
- Procurement thresholds: Finance splits vendor sign-off as follows: <$20k/month (finance ops), $20–60k/month (VP finance approval), $60k+/board notification + legal review. For a $60k+ monthly commitment we typically need the legal/compliance review (2–3 weeks) + VP sign-off.
- Lead times: Legal wants standard security attachments (SOC 2, data retention, KMS details) and an indemnity clause preview. 

Looping in Sarah from procurement to coordinate next steps. Sarah — we may be aiming for a $40–75k/month budget band initially, leaning to $60k+/mo in Q2 if adoption tracks. Can procurement start a standard vendor intake so we can understand timing?

Chris

--
Chris Nolan
Head of Product, Vyron Payments
chris.nolan@vyronpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0789
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@vyronpay.com>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@vyronpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + budget band confirmation (post-demo)

Thanks Chris — that is super helpful and aligns with what we expected. A couple of clarifications and a pricing breakdown you can share with procurement: 

Unit economics examples (rounded, illustrative):
- Hosted API (no commit): $320 per 1M tokens -> If you hit 60M tokens/mo that’s ~$19.2k/mo.
- Dedicated / reserved (6–12mo commit) entry tier: $220 per 1M tokens -> 60M tokens/mo = ~$13.2k/mo.
- Committed enterprise tier (annual+$ commit + SLA): $150 per 1M tokens -> 60M tokens/mo = ~$9k/mo.

Note: these are before any negotiated volume or annual-commit discounts. For the ranges you gave (~40–75k monthly target) it sounds like you may be budgeting for additional services, multi-region redundancy, or higher-cost model variants. If your procurement threshold for VP approval is $20–60k, then a conservative path is to aim for an initial committed tier that keeps net spend below $60k/mo while giving headroom to scale to the $60k+ band in Q2.

Procurement asks we can handle from our side:
- We’ll attach SOC 2 report and data retention/KMS summary in the vendor intake.
- I’ll share a cleaned pricing sheet with three scenarios (hosted / dedicated / enterprise commit) and an example PO template.
- DocuSign SOW link: https://www.docusign.com/link/RDW-2345-SOW (draft will be editable for legal redlines).

If helpful, here are two quick scenario examples for your finance team to model (monthly totals incl. estimated infra & support add-on):
- Conservative: 50M tokens @ $220/1M = $11k/mo -> quarterly PO of ~$33k (fits <$20k/month? No, but within VP approval band).
- Aggressive: 110M tokens @ $150/1M = $16.5k/mo -> this assumes enterprise commit discount and will require legal + board notification only if you push to $60k+/mo after adding other services.

Next steps:
1) Chris/Sarah: confirm target procurement band (which approval level you want to hit initially).
2) I’ll send a cleaned pricing sheet + SOC2 + PO template by EOD.
3) If procurement wants, we can schedule a 30-min intake with our finance/security SME to speed approvals.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to run the scenarios with finance (I can bring Marissa).

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Vyron pricing band / discount ask

Rishi — quick internal note. Sounds like Vyron is targeting the $40–75k/mo band with VP approval in the middle. If they push to an initial $60k+ commit we should consider offering a one-time onboarding credit + 15% off list for the first 6 months in exchange for an annual commit. Confirm you want me to approve that concession. Also confirm whether the SOC2 + KMS doc we have is the latest (I’ll attach if needed).

If you want to move fast I can pre-authorize the 15% for deals with deal_id RDW-2345 pending legal review.

-Marissa
